nodes.title: Cloud governance: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Governance is the set of policies and guardrails that keep a cloud account safe and on-budget as it scales from one engineer to a hundred. Think tagging standards, budget alerts, organizational policies, and the multi-account strategy.

flashcards.front: Why use multiple accounts (an Organization) instead of one big account?
flashcards.back: Blast-radius isolation: a compromised prod account doesn't leak into dev. Billing clarity: per-team or per-environment cost reports. Quota independence: prod doesn't share API limits with sandbox. Service Control Policies (AWS) / management groups (Azure) enforce 'no one can disable CloudTrail' across the whole org.

flashcards.front: What is a Service Control Policy (SCP)?
flashcards.back: An AWS Organizations policy that sets the maximum permissions any IAM identity in a member account can have. Even if a user's IAM policy grants `s3:*`, an SCP denying `s3:DeleteBucket` overrides it. SCPs are guardrails, not grants — they only restrict.

flashcards.front: Tagging strategy — name three high-leverage tags.
flashcards.back: (1) Owner / team — who pays and who to page. (2) Environment (prod/staging/dev) — drives access controls and lifecycle. (3) Cost-center / project — for chargeback. Tags are free and infinitely valuable for cost allocation and automation; enforce them with policies.

A pre-baked multi-account setup with security baselines: org with master + audit + log-archive + workload accounts, CloudTrail / Config enabled everywhere, SSO wired up, network templates ready. AWS Control Tower / Azure Landing Zones / GCP setup automate this so you start on a safe foundation, not bare cloud.

pairs.stem: An architect needs to design a solution to prevent accidental deletion of a critical Azure SQL Database. Even subscription owners should not be able to delete it without explicit action. Which control achieves this?
pairs.option: Apply a CanNotDelete resource lock to the Azure SQL Database.

pairs.stem: An architect needs to grant a team of junior developers access to create and manage resources within a specific resource group, but prevent them from modifying any IAM/RBAC assignments. Which RBAC role combination achieves least-privilege?
pairs.option: Assign the Contributor role at the resource group scope.

pairs.stem: A large enterprise needs to enforce that all Azure resources must be deployed only in specific regions (West Europe and North Europe) across 80 subscriptions. New subscriptions added in the future must automatically comply. What is the MOST scalable approach?
pairs.option: Create a custom RBAC role in each subscription that restricts deployment to those regions

pairs.stem: A company's operations team needs to collect OS-level performance metrics (custom memory counters, application logs) from 500 Azure VMs and on-premises servers into a central workspace for dashboards and alerts. Which Azure Monitor component collects this data?
pairs.option: Azure Monitor Metrics — collects platform-level metrics from Azure resources without agents

pairs.stem: A solutions architect must design an identity solution for a company with 10,000 on-premises Active Directory users who need SSO access to Azure resources and Microsoft 365. The company cannot allow password hashes to be stored in the cloud for compliance reasons. Which hybrid identity method satisfies this requirement?
pairs.option: Azure AD Connect with ADFS federation — authentication happens on-premises via ADFS; Azure AD acts as relying party

pairs.stem: A solutions architect is designing a monitoring strategy. The application team needs to detect performance regressions in a .NET web application running on Azure App Service, including dependency call durations, exception rates, and user session tracking. Which monitoring solution is most appropriate?
pairs.option: Application Insights connected to the App Service.

pairs.stem: A solutions architect must design connectivity from an on-premises datacenter to Azure with guaranteed bandwidth, low latency, and consistent throughput for a financial services application transferring large data sets. Which connectivity option is most appropriate?
pairs.option: Azure ExpressRoute with a dedicated private connection through a network service provider.

pairs.stem: An architect needs to design a backup strategy for 200 Azure VMs across 5 subscriptions, ensuring all VMs are backed up daily with 30-day retention. A central team must be able to monitor backup compliance from a single dashboard. What is the recommended design?
pairs.option: Deploy a third-party backup solution from Azure Marketplace that supports multi-subscription management

pairs.stem: A company needs to move 500 TB of data from on-premises NAS to Azure Blob Storage. The internet connection is only 100 Mbps and encrypting 500 TB over the internet would take 46+ days. Which Azure data transfer service eliminates this constraint?
pairs.option: Azure ExpressRoute with 10 Gbps circuit for bulk data transfer

pairs.stem: A company is migrating a monolithic .NET Framework 4.8 application to Azure. The application cannot be refactored and requires full IIS control, custom GAC assemblies, and Windows Registry access. Which compute option is appropriate?
pairs.option: Azure Virtual Machines running Windows Server.

pairs.stem: A company is designing its Azure storage strategy. Large files (video content, 50-500 GB each) will be uploaded once and accessed frequently for the first 30 days, rarely for the next 60 days, then almost never after 90 days. What lifecycle management policy minimizes cost?
pairs.option: Configure a Blob lifecycle policy: transition to Cool tier at 30 days.

pairs.stem: A company is planning to migrate 200 on-premises servers to Azure. The migration team needs to discover and assess all servers (VMware, physical, Hyper-V) to understand dependencies, right-size VM SKUs in Azure, and estimate monthly costs before migrating. Which Azure service provides this assessment capability?
pairs.option: Azure Monitor with Dependency Map to discover server relationships

nodes.title: Part 3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 3. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An e-commerce application experiences Black Friday spikes of 100x normal traffic. The application is hosted on Azure App Service. The architect wants the application to scale out automatically based on HTTP request queue length, not just CPU. Which autoscaling approach enables custom metric scaling?
flashcards.back: Azure App Service exposes custom metrics including HttpQueueLength (number of requests waiting in the HTTP queue) that can trigger autoscale rules. This metric is more relevant for queue-based bottlenecks than CPU — a healthy app might have low CPU but a growing HTTP queue if I/O-bound. Autoscale rules: scale out when HttpQueueLength > 10 (add instances), scale in when < 1 (remove instances). This provides more responsive scaling than CPU for web workloads. Traffic Manager is DNS-level, not application-level autoscaling. scale out when queue length > 10, scale in when < 1

flashcards.front: A solutions architect needs to design an API layer for a microservices application. The API must support rate limiting, request/response transformation, authentication (JWT validation), developer portal for API documentation, and monetization through subscription keys. Which Azure service provides all of these capabilities?
flashcards.back: Azure API Management is specifically designed as a full-lifecycle API management platform. Key features: Inbound/outbound policies (rate limiting, IP filtering, JWT validation, header transformation), OAuth2/OpenID Connect integration, developer portal (auto-generated API documentation, subscription management), product tiers with subscription keys for monetization, built-in analytics, and backend load balancing. Application Gateway and Front Door are network-layer load balancers without API management capabilities. Azure Functions require building all cross-cutting concerns from scratch. provides a full API gateway with policies for rate limiting, transformation, JWT validation, OAuth2, developer portal, product subscriptions, and analytics

flashcards.front: An architect is designing a solution for an application that processes financial transactions. Each transaction must be processed exactly once, in order, and failures must be retried without duplicate processing. Which messaging pattern is most appropriate?
flashcards.back: Service Bus Queues provide exactly-once, ordered processing through: (1) Message Sessions — enables FIFO ordering per session key (e.g., account ID), ensuring transactions for the same account are processed in order, (2) Duplicate detection — if a message is resent with the same MessageId within a configurable window, Service Bus discards the duplicate, (3) Dead-letter queue (DLQ) for messages that fail after max retries. Event Hubs is optimized for high-throughput telemetry streaming, not reliable ordered business transactions. Storage Queue has no ordering guarantee and no duplicate detection. dead-letter queue for failures, and duplicate detection enabled

flashcards.front: A developer team wants to deploy a web application using containers to Azure with no Kubernetes management overhead, automatic HTTPS, built-in scale-to-zero, and support for sidecar containers. Which Azure service provides all of these?
flashcards.back: Azure Container Apps is the modern PaaS for microservices containers without Kubernetes management. It provides: KEDA-based autoscaling including scale-to-zero, built-in HTTPS ingress with auto-managed TLS certificates, sidecar container support (Dapr integration), revision management for blue-green deployments, and support for event-driven architectures. ACI is for single containers without built-in HTTP ingress or KEDA scaling. App Service supports containers but doesn't support sidecars natively. AKS requires cluster management. supporting autoscaling including scale-to-zero, HTTPS ingress, and sidecar containers without Kubernetes management

pairs.stem: An architect needs to design an Azure AD identity solution that allows external business partners to sign in using their own organizational credentials (Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, or SAML IdP) to access a shared portal. Partner users should not have accounts created in the host directory. Which feature enables this?
pairs.option: Azure AD External Identities B2B collaboration.

pairs.stem: An architect is designing a solution that will run thousands of short-lived (5-15 second) background tasks triggered by messages in an Azure Storage Queue. The code is simple, stateless, and must scale to zero when the queue is empty to minimize costs. What is the most cost-effective compute option?
pairs.option: Azure Logic Apps consumption plan triggered by Storage Queue

pairs.stem: A developer team wants to deploy a web application using containers to Azure with no Kubernetes management overhead, automatic HTTPS, built-in scale-to-zero, and support for sidecar containers. Which Azure service provides all of these?
pairs.option: Azure App Service with Docker container deployment

pairs.stem: A solutions architect needs to design an API layer for a microservices application. The API must support rate limiting, request/response transformation, authentication (JWT validation), developer portal for API documentation, and monetization through subscription keys. Which Azure service provides all of these capabilities?
pairs.option: Azure API Management (APIM).

pairs.stem: A startup is designing its first Azure application — a web app with a REST API backend and a SQL database. The team has 2 developers and needs to be productive with minimal infrastructure management. The expected load is 100-500 users/day for the first 6 months. What is the most appropriate architecture?
pairs.option: Azure App Service (Free or Basic tier) for the web app and API.

pairs.stem: An e-commerce application experiences Black Friday spikes of 100x normal traffic. The application is hosted on Azure App Service. The architect wants the application to scale out automatically based on HTTP request queue length, not just CPU. Which autoscaling approach enables custom metric scaling?
pairs.option: Azure App Service automatic scaling (preview) based on HTTP latency metrics

nodes.title: Role-based access control: Key Ideas
nodes.content: RBAC assigns permissions to roles, then users to roles — a layer of indirection that scales. Azure's RBAC, AWS's IAM, Kubernetes RBAC, and GCP's IAM all share the same mental model. Mastering one transfers directly to the others.

flashcards.front: Why use roles instead of granting permissions to users directly?
flashcards.back: Roles separate WHO from WHAT. Add a person to a role, they inherit the permissions. Remove them, they lose access instantly. Auditing: 'who can read prod?' becomes 'who's in the prod-readers role?' instead of scanning thousands of user-level policies. Onboarding/offboarding becomes role membership changes, not 500 permission grants.

flashcards.front: What's the difference between a built-in role and a custom role?
flashcards.back: Built-in: cloud-provided, covers common patterns (Owner, Contributor, Reader, Storage Admin). Can't be modified. Custom: you define the exact actions allowed — pick when built-ins are too broad or too narrow. Cost of custom roles: maintenance — every new service adds actions you may need to add.

flashcards.front: Scope — why is it as important as the role?
flashcards.back: Same role at different scopes = wildly different power. 'Contributor' at the subscription scope = god mode on the whole subscription. 'Contributor' on one resource group = limited to that group's resources. Always scope at the smallest unit that's practical — never grant subscription-level if resource-group-level works.

flashcards.front: RBAC vs ABAC — when do you need attributes?
flashcards.back: RBAC: permissions tied to fixed roles. Works great until you need rules like 'engineers can read their own team's resources but not others'. ABAC (attribute-based) evaluates request attributes (user.team, resource.team) at runtime. Most clouds support both — start with RBAC, add ABAC tags when the role explosion becomes painful.

pairs.stem: A company's compliance team requires that ALL changes to Azure resources (creates, updates, deletes) in their production subscription be logged and retained for 1 year. The logs must be queryable. What is the correct configuration?
pairs.option: Configure a Diagnostic Setting at the subscription level to export Activity Logs to a Log Analytics workspace with 1-year retention.

pairs.stem: A company needs to deploy a highly available web application in Azure with connection-based session affinity (sticky sessions) and SSL offloading. The web tier has 10 VMs in the same VNet. Which load balancer supports these requirements?
pairs.option: Azure Application Gateway.

pairs.stem: An architect needs to design a solution where an Azure Function needs to call multiple Azure services (Blob Storage, Cosmos DB, Key Vault) without storing any credentials or connection strings in the function's application settings. Which identity pattern is recommended?
pairs.option: Create a service principal in Azure AD with certificates stored in Key Vault for authentication

pairs.stem: A solutions architect needs to design a globally distributed application that caches frequently read data to minimize database load. The cache must be highly available within a region and should share no single point of failure between cache and primary database. Which Azure caching solution supports replication within a region for HA?
pairs.option: Azure Cosmos DB integrated cache for sub-millisecond reads

pairs.stem: A company needs a storage solution for SMB file shares that Windows VMs access like traditional on-premises network drives. The solution must support Active Directory authentication for access control and provide 99.99% availability SLA. Which Azure service provides this?
pairs.option: Azure Files Premium with SMB 3.0 protocol.

pairs.stem: A company wants to build a serverless event-driven architecture where order placement events trigger inventory updates, billing, and notification workflows independently. If one downstream service is temporarily unavailable, the event must be retried without losing it. Which Azure messaging service is designed for this pattern?
pairs.option: Azure Event Hubs — high-throughput streaming for real-time analytics on order events
